newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to tell G7 recovery becoming sustainable.
newsitem.headline: Japan to tell G7 recovery becoming sustainable.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Wataru Kubo told a news conference on Wednesday that he would tell Group of Seven (G7) partners on September 28 that Japan's economy is gradually moving towards self-sustainable recovery centred on private demand.

Looking at the gross domestic product figures for April-June released recently, Japan's economy was still growing, although the growth was not as high as that seen in the January to March period, he said.
Kubo said that a report by the International Monetary Fund also said Japan's economy has been recovering.
"I think the international organisations have judged Japan's economic growth as at the higher end of that of the G7 nations," Kubo said.

Asked what Japan was going to tell G7 finance ministers and central bankers about its own economy, Kubo said: "The economy is gradually moving towards self-sustainable recovery centering on private demand."
"But we have to keep close watch on what kind of impact our fiscal policy has on consumption," he said.
Japanese cabinet ministers have decided to go ahead with a planned increase in the consumption tax to five percent from the current three starting from April 1997, to make up for previous tax cuts.
Kubo said it was "impossible" to overturn the government decision to increase the tax and added that so far, no study had shown it would do any severe damage to the economy.
Kubo said he would like to meet U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky in Washington on September 29 to discuss a bilateral insurance dispute.
